All simulations use PLEXOS version 9.0r9 with the Gurobi version 9.5.1 solver. We simulate the impact of using DLC-LE to manage EV charging by partitioning the EV load into nonparticipating fixed and participating flexible portions and dispatching the flexible load in Stage 0. Nonparticipating EV load is aggregated into regional, unmanaged profiles. Sample vehicles participating in DLC EVMC are assigned to one of 19 ISO-NE dispatch zones, their flexibility is aggregated per dispatch zone as described in Section 2.3, and the resulting flexibility models are instantiated as PLEXOS pumped storage hydropower units. Stage 0 then optimizes these battery-like pumped storage hydropower units alongside supply-side resources. The resulting aggregate profiles are used as perfect-foresight forecasts of the actual DLC-LE EVMC response in Stages 1 and 2. The price-responsive dispatch mechanism simulations (RTP and TOU) also partition EV load into participating (flexible) and nonparticipating (fixed) portions. Fixed EV load is aggregated by county and assigned to the nearest node. Participating price-responsive EVs minimize their charging costs based on the flexibility constraints Eqs. 2.3–2.5, 2.9, 2.10, and 2.12, and their individual vehicle parameter values , , and . We simulate two forecast types for the price-responsive dispatch mechanisms: no-foresight and perfect-foresight, by using different Stage 1 results as input into Stage 2. Stage 2 always uses the actual price-responsive EV load simulated for the specified mechanism (RTP or TOU), flexibility type (within-session or within-week), and participation level.
